description: Make Typr (Tauri v2 dictation app, repo root = this directory, C:/Users/guruv/tools/typr) match Wispr Flow / SuperWhisper UX quality. THE SPEC IS docs/RESEARCH-wispr-superwhisper.md - read it before every story; section numbers below refer to it. Architecture rules that apply to EVERY story: overlay animations are transform/opacity ONLY (GPU compositable, no width/height/layout animation), no polling loops anywhere (event-driven: global-shortcut events, Rust-emitted events, WinEventHook; a single rAF loop may run ONLY while the overlay is in the listening state), all state flows Rust -> overlay via the existing eval/emit path, the webview is a pure renderer. DO NOT remove or weaken src-tauri/.cargo/config.toml or the lib-patch/ and sdk-patch/ folders - they work around a damaged VS/SDK install; without them the build breaks. Quality gate for every story: 'npm run build' (tsc + vite) passes AND 'cargo check' inside src-tauri passes. Do not run 'npm run tauri build' except in the final story (it is slow). The app currently works end to end: settings window renders, whisper-server sidecar starts, hotkey CmdOrCtrl+Shift+Space records and pastes.

userStories.title: Fixed-size overlay host window with internal data-state pill morphing
userStories.description: As a user, I want the pill to morph between states without any window flicker. Per research section 1 and 7.1: make the overlay a FIXED 440x160 transparent host window (bottom-center) and remove all per-state OS window resizing from recorder.rs update_overlay; instead the pill morphs entirely inside the webview driven by a data-state attribute on the pill root. Pre-mount ALL states in overlay.html (idle lozenge ~64x12px, listening layout, processing layout, done tick) and crossfade with opacity + translate/scale only, 120-180ms, per section 7.2. update_overlay evals exactly one thing: document.getElementById('mic').dataset.state = '<state>'.
acceptanceCriteria: src-tauri/src/main.rs creates the overlay at 440x160 and never resizes it; recorder.rs contains no set_size/set_position calls in update_overlay
src/overlay.html has all states pre-mounted in the DOM, visibility toggled purely by CSS [data-state] rules using only opacity and transform
Idle state renders as a small dark lozenge (~64x12), not the old 40px mic circle
npm run build passes and cargo check (in src-tauri) passes
userStories.notes: Fixed 440x160 host; pill states idle/listening/processing/done pre-mounted in overlay.html, crossfaded via #mic[data-state] with opacity+transform only. update_overlay is a single dataset.state eval.

userStories.title: Default click-through overlay with Rust cursor hit-test toggling
userStories.description: As a user, I want the big transparent host window to never block my clicks, while the pill itself stays hoverable and draggable. Per research section 1 (hover row): set set_ignore_cursor_events(true) by default; install a WH_MOUSE_LL low-level mouse hook in Rust (windows crate) that computes whether the cursor is inside the pill's screen rect (pill rect = known CSS position within the fixed host window + window outer_position) and flips ignore_cursor_events off when inside, on when outside. Keep data-tauri-drag-region dragging working when interactive; after a drag ends, clamp the window into the monitor work area and persist {x,y} into the existing Settings, restoring on startup.
acceptanceCriteria: Overlay window is click-through by default and interactive only when the cursor is over the pill rect (hook-driven, no JS polling)
Dragging the pill still works, and the saved position is written to the settings JSON and reapplied on next launch, clamped to the work area
The mouse hook is installed once at setup and uninstalled on exit; no timer or polling loop is introduced
npm run build passes and cargo check passes
userStories.notes: Click-through by default (set_ignore_cursor_events(true)); WH_MOUSE_LL hook in pill_hittest.rs flips interactivity over the 200x48 pill rect (cached atomics, updated on Moved/ScaleFactorChanged events). Drag-end (LBUTTONUP in the same hook) clamps to work area and persists overlayX/overlayY; restored + clamped on startup. save_settings re-asserts the Rust-owned position over stale frontend snapshots.

userStories.title: Live honest waveform driven by real mic RMS at 30Hz
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see real waveform bars while I speak so I trust it is hearing me. Per research sections 1 (listening row) and 7.3: in the cpal capture callback in audio.rs, compute RMS per ~33ms chunk and emit a throttled 'audio-level' event (single float) at most 30Hz to the overlay. overlay.html renders 14 pre-created bar divs; a single rAF loop, running ONLY while data-state=listening, maps the latest level to per-bar transform: scaleY() values (center bars taller, randomized per-bar weighting set once at load, not per frame). If level stays below a silence threshold for 600ms, ease all bars to scaleY(0.08) - the honest flatline.
acceptanceCriteria: audio.rs emits 'audio-level' events at a throttled rate (max ~30/s) only while recording
overlay.html animates bars with transform: scaleY only, from a single rAF loop that starts on entering listening state and stops on leaving it
Silence for 600ms visibly flattens the bars (threshold logic present in overlay JS)
npm run build passes and cargo check passes
userStories.notes: cpal callback in audio.rs accumulates sum-of-squares and emits 'audio-level' (single RMS float) via emit_to("overlay") at >=33ms spacing; stream lifetime = recording, so no gating flag. overlay.html: window-scoped listener (emit_to does not reach target-Any listeners), 14 fixed center-weighted per-bar weights set at load, one rAF loop gated by a MutationObserver on data-state, scaleY-only writes, 600ms silence eases bars to 0.08.

userStories.title: Instant keydown feedback: state + ping before any heavy work
userStories.description: As a user, I want the pill to react the instant I press the hotkey. Per research section 2 (bottom note) and 7.4: on ShortcutState::Pressed the handler must, in order and before any other work: (1) set overlay state to listening, (2) play a short pre-loaded start ping (use rodio or windows PlaySound with a bundled small wav in src-tauri/sounds/, decoded/loaded once at startup), (3) start capture. Add a stop ping on finalize. Add an 'Interaction sounds' boolean to Settings (default true) respected by both pings. No blocking I/O (file reads, device enumeration) may happen on the hotkey path.
acceptanceCriteria: Overlay state change and ping dispatch occur before capture start in the Pressed handler, with the sound assets loaded at app setup, not on the hotkey path
Settings gains interaction_sounds (default true) and both pings respect it
cargo check passes and npm run build passes
userStories.notes: sounds.rs (new): start/stop pings embedded via include_bytes! ('static), played with winmm PlaySoundW SND_ASYNC|SND_MEMORY|SND_NODEFAULT — zero hotkey latency. Pressed handler does state-set + play_start synchronously BEFORE spawning the capture async task; play_stop at both finalize points. Settings +interactionSounds/+overlayVisible (camelCase wire via serde rename, default true, compat tests). save_settings applies overlay show/hide immediately; startup honors overlay_visible.

userStories.title: One key, three gestures: tap toggles, hold is push-to-talk
userStories.description: As a user, I want Wispr's gesture model on a single hotkey. Per research section 2: keydown always starts capture immediately. If keyup arrives under 300ms, treat as a tap: stay recording (hands-free). If held past 300ms, keyup stops and transcribes (push-to-talk). A second tap while hands-free recording stops and transcribes. Replace the current recording_mode toggle/push-to-talk setting semantics with this unified model (keep the setting as an override: 'auto' default plus the two legacy explicit modes).
acceptanceCriteria: Hotkey handler in main.rs implements tap-vs-hold discrimination with a 300ms threshold and second-tap stop, with no sleep/blocking on the event thread
Settings recording_mode supports 'auto' (new default), 'toggle', 'push-to-talk'; existing saved settings still load
cargo check passes and npm run build passes
userStories.notes: main.rs: 'auto' branch added alongside the existing toggle/push-to-talk (unchanged). Gesture state is ONE enum (HotkeyGesture: Idle/Pressed(Instant)/HandsFree) behind ONE Mutex on AppState (hotkey_gesture) - deliberately not two independently-locked fields, so the read-decide-mutate step for a Pressed/Released pair is a single atomic transaction (code review caught that two separate locks let a fast second tap observe an in-between combination that could never occur in real wall-clock order). Pressed: if Ready, starts capture immediately (sync overlay+ping, same as US-004) and stores Pressed(now); if Recording and gesture==HandsFree (second tap), swaps it to Idle and stops+transcribes immediately, no keyup wait. Released: locks once, matches Pressed(t) - <300ms elapsed sets HandsFree (keeps recording, hands-free), >=300ms sets Idle and stops+transcribes (PTT); Idle/HandsFree here means this Released follows an already-finalized second tap - no-op. No sleeps; tap/hold decided by comparing Instant::now() at the real event boundaries. settings.rs default recording_mode is now 'auto' (explicit saved 'toggle'/'push-to-talk' still load literally - see test_load_pre_us004_config_gives_true_defaults assertion). index.html/main.ts gained a third 'Auto' toggle button in Recording Mode, wired the same way as the existing two. Reviewed by code-reviewer agent before commit (HIGH finding on lock consolidation fixed; remaining MEDIUM/LOW are pre-existing architectural tradeoffs shared by all recording modes, not new in this story).

userStories.title: Esc cancel with 30-second discard guard
userStories.description: As a user, I want Esc to cancel a dictation, but not to lose a long one by accident. Per research sections 1 (cancel guard) and 2: register Esc as a global shortcut ONLY while recording (register on state->Recording, unregister on leaving). Esc under 30s of recording cancels instantly (discard audio, state->idle). Over 30s, first Esc puts the pill in a 'confirm-discard' state (pre-mounted layout: 'Discard? press Esc again'); second Esc within 3s discards, otherwise recording continues.
acceptanceCriteria: Esc is not globally registered when idle (verify register/unregister calls are tied to recording state transitions)
Recording duration is tracked in Rust; the 30s guard and 3s confirm window are implemented with tokio sleeps/timestamps, no polling
overlay.html has the pre-mounted confirm-discard state following the same data-state crossfade pattern
cargo check passes and npm run build passes
userStories.notes: recorder.rs: Escape is registered via arm_cancel_shortcut() only from inside start_recording (Ready->Recording) and unregistered from both cancel_recording and the top of stop_and_transcribe (leaving Recording) - never registered while idle. Recording start stamps recording_started_at: Arc<Mutex<Option<Instant>>>; a CancelGuard enum (None/ConfirmDiscard(Instant)) tracks the confirm-discard prompt. Esc under 30s elapsed -> cancel_recording (new AudioRecorder::cancel() drops the cpal stream and clears samples without writing a WAV). Esc past 30s: first press arms confirm-discard (sets overlay data-state via set_overlay_state, a small refactor pulled out of update_overlay) and spawns a tokio::time::sleep(3s) auto-revert task debounced against a fresher arm/clear via an armed_at Instant token (no polling); a second Esc while armed discards immediately. IMPORTANT (verified against tauri-plugin-global-shortcut 2.3.1 + global-hotkey 0.7.0 source, and confirmed by a code-reviewer pass): the plugin's GlobalHotKeyEvent dispatch holds a lock on its own internal shortcuts map for the entire duration of a shortcut's handler closure (on Windows this closure runs on the main thread's WndProc), so calling global_shortcut().register/unregister/on_shortcut SYNCHRONOUSLY from inside that closure would self-deadlock (re-locking the same non-reentrant Mutex) and freeze the whole app's message pump. Every register/unregister triggered by an Esc press is therefore deferred via tauri::async_runtime::spawn, executing after the closure has returned and released the lock. A code-reviewer pass also caught (and this was fixed) a real race in cancel_recording: state must NOT flip to Ready (the sole gate start_recording checks) until AFTER unregister(Escape) completes, otherwise a rapid cancel-then-restart could let a new recording start arming its own Escape registration while the old one's teardown is still in flight, silently leaving Esc unregistered for the new session. The 3s auto-revert timer also double-checks state==Recording (not just the CancelGuard token) before reverting the overlay, so a confirmed discard can't be visually clobbered back to 'listening' by a losing-the-race timer.

userStories.title: Clipboard-respecting paste with fallback and paste-last shortcut
userStories.description: As a user, I want dictation to paste without destroying my clipboard, into the RIGHT app, and a rescue path when paste fails. Per research section 3: in paste.rs save the current clipboard text, write the transcript, synthesize Ctrl+V, wait briefly, restore the saved clipboard; write the transient transcript with the ExcludeClipboardContentFromMonitorProcessing and CF_CLIPBOARD_VIEWER_IGNORE formats so clipboard managers skip it. FOCUS GUARD (from a real user bug on 2026-07-19: transcription took long enough that the user switched apps, and the transcript was pasted into the wrong app; the user wants the text to land in the window that was focused when they dictated): capture the foreground window handle (GetForegroundWindow) at the moment recording stops; at paste time, if the current foreground window differs, RE-FOCUS the captured window (SetForegroundWindow, with the AttachThreadInput trick if needed since Windows restricts stealing focus) and paste there; only if refocus fails (window gone/cloaked), leave the transcript on the clipboard and show the paste-fallback state instead. If paste fails, same fallback: transcript stays on clipboard, overlay state 'paste-fallback' (pre-mounted pill state with a Paste hint) until next state change. Register global shortcut Shift+Alt+Z to re-insert the last transcript (store last transcript in AppState).
acceptanceCriteria: paste.rs implements save -> write(with exclusion formats) -> Ctrl+V -> restore, and restores only on success per Wispr's documented behavior
When the foreground window changed between end-of-recording and paste time, the originally focused window is re-focused and receives the paste; clipboard + paste-fallback only when refocus fails
paste-fallback state exists in overlay.html and is triggered on paste failure
Shift+Alt+Z re-pastes the last transcript; last transcript stored in AppState
cargo check passes and npm run build passes

userStories.title: Processing budget UX: late processing state, done tick, status dot
userStories.description: As a user, I want short dictations to feel instant. Per research sections 1 and 7.5: after capture stops, only switch the pill to 'processing' if transcription has not completed within 300ms (Rust-side tokio timer; if the result lands first, skip processing state entirely). On success show the 'done' tick state for ~400ms then relax to idle. Add SuperWhisper's status dot to the pill corner (8px, opacity-crossfaded colors): yellow while whisper-server is starting/model loading, blue during processing, green on done, driven by existing Rust state.
acceptanceCriteria: Processing state is skipped when transcription completes under 300ms (timer logic in Rust, not JS)
done state auto-relaxes to idle after ~400ms; status dot colors driven by events, changed via CSS variables and opacity only
cargo check passes and npm run build passes
userStories.notes: WEBVIEW SIDE ALREADY PRE-MOUNTED in overlay.html: 8px .status-dot on listening/processing/done layers, colors via [data-dot] rules (starting=yellow, processing=blue, done=green, off=hidden), driven by a window-scoped 'status-dot' event listener (payload 'starting'|'processing'|'done'|'off') that sets mic.dataset.dot. Rust work only: the 300ms late-processing timer, 400ms done relax, and emit_to("overlay", "status-dot", ...) at the right lifecycle points.

userStories.title: Pill interactions: hover emphasis, left-click opens app, right-click quick menu
userStories.description: As a user, I want the pill to react like a real control (user spec 2026-07-19): HOVER makes it expand slightly and become fully solid/opaque (strengthen the existing :hover rule: opacity to 1.0 and background alpha to ~0.95, plus the scale-up, transform/opacity only). LEFT-CLICK opens/focuses the main Typr settings window (a click is a press-release under ~200ms with no drag movement; a longer press or movement is the existing drag). Per research section 1 (click actions): contextmenu (right-click) opens an in-webview menu growing upward from the pill (transform-origin bottom center, scale 0.95->1 + opacity, 120ms) with items: Hide for 1 hour, Paste last transcript, Settings, Quit. Hide-for-1-hour hides the overlay window and un-hides via a single Rust tokio sleep task (hotkey keeps working while hidden). Quit exits the app cleanly (killing whisper-server as the existing exit handler does). Menu closes on outside click, Esc, or item activation. The 440x160 host gives the menu room; menu must stay within the host window bounds.
acceptanceCriteria: Hovering the pill visibly expands it and makes it fully opaque, via transform/opacity only
A quick left-click (no drag) shows and focuses the main Typr window; dragging still moves the pill
Right-clicking the pill opens the menu with the four items, animated with transform/opacity only, fully inside the host window
Hide for 1 hour hides the overlay, dictation still works while hidden, and it reappears after the timer without any polling
Settings shows and focuses the main window; Quit fully exits including the whisper-server child
npm run build passes and cargo check passes
userStories.notes: MENU BACKING DONE (this pass): main.rs adds the 4 #[tauri::command]s the pre-mounted quick-menu already invokes by name (tauri.core.invoke(data-action)) - menu_hide_hour (hide() + tauri::async_runtime::spawn(tokio::time::sleep(3600s)) then re-show, respecting settings.overlay_visible so a user who separately turned the overlay off in Settings stays hidden; hotkey/recording never depended on overlay visibility so dictation keeps working while hidden), menu_paste_last (Recorder::get_last_transcript() from US-007, then the SAME paste path: paste::capture_foreground_window() + paste::paste_text() - no second paste implementation, paste.rs untouched; sets pill data-state to the existing 'done'/'paste-fallback' states on Pasted/Fallback; a real no-op returning Err when there is no last transcript yet, not a fake success), menu_open_settings (get_webview_window("main").show()+set_focus()), menu_quit (app.exit(0), which drives the existing RunEvent::Exit handler that already kills whisper-server and uninstalls the pill hit-test hook - no duplicate cleanup). All 4 registered in generate_handler!. STILL OPEN for this story (out of scope for this pass, left as-is): hover emphasis, left-click-vs-drag opening the main window, and hit-rect widening via data-menu=open in pill_hittest.rs - none of these are dead controls (hover/menu-open/close already work in the webview; left-click behavior simply isn't backed by a discriminator yet, a gap not a fake affordance) but the story is not fully done until those land.

userStories.title: Recording waveform: solid flat stroke, heart-rate/radar motion (no gradient, no halo)
userStories.description: As a user, I want the recording waveform to read as a SOLID line that sweeps like a heart-rate monitor or a radar detecting for voice, not a glowing gradient sine. TJ rejected the current look twice: 'why is it gradient?' then 'the wavelength is still a gradient color and not a solid deep color and its not animated like a heart rate monitor / or a radar detecting for voice'. Root cause of the perceived gradient was ctx.shadowBlur painting a fading halo around an already-flat stroke; that has been removed, so this story is about MOTION and HUE. Replace the travelling sine in src/overlay.html with an ECG-style trace: a mostly-flat baseline punctuated by a sharp QRS-like spike whose height is driven by the live mic RMS, sweeping left-to-right with a leading edge, OR a radar sweep reading of the same signal. Keep the existing rAF-only-while-listening rule and the real audio-level event as the amplitude source - never synthesise fake activity.
acceptanceCriteria: src/overlay.html canvas renderer draws an ECG/radar-style trace, not a continuous sine; amplitude still comes from the real 'audio-level' RMS event
ctx.shadowBlur is NOT set anywhere in the waveform renderer (a blurred halo reads as a gradient)
Stroke colour is a single flat value read from one :root custom property; no createLinearGradient, no per-segment colour variation
Measured contrast of the stroke against --pill-recording-bg is >= 4.5:1; record the measured number in the story notes
The rAF loop still runs ONLY while data-state=listening and stops on leaving it
Silence still visibly flatlines the trace
npm run build passes and cargo check passes (run unpiped, check the exit code)
cdp-smoke (typr-e2e) reports 25/25 against the freshly built exe
userStories.notes: Hue is NOT settled: TJ asked for a 'solid deep color' but the existing cyan was chosen for measured contrast against the red recording pill, and deep hues on red contrast poorly. Implement the motion change, keep the colour behind a single token, and surface the measured contrast so TJ can pick the final hue. Do not silently invent a hue and call it done.

userStories.title: Whisper-vs-talking level indicator against the real mic threshold
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see whether I am currently above or below the level threshold the app uses, so I know if I am whispering too quietly to be transcribed. TJ: 'if the microphone or whatever threshold number you have set for distinguishing between whispering vs talking could you display that indicator between whispering and talking. talking would be higher than the threshold number you have set.' Find the ACTUAL silence/level threshold constant already used in the codebase (audio.rs RMS handling and the overlay's silence-flatline logic) and surface it - do not invent a new number. Show a small indicator during recording that reads whispering (below threshold) vs talking (at or above), driven by the same live audio-level event.
acceptanceCriteria: The threshold value displayed is read from the existing constant in the codebase, not a newly invented literal; cite the file and constant in the story notes
During recording the overlay shows a whispering/talking indicator that flips based on the live 'audio-level' value vs that threshold
The indicator is driven by the existing audio-level event only; no new polling loop and no second rAF loop
Indicator uses transform/opacity only so the fixed-size overlay window is untouched
If the level source is unavailable the indicator renders a neutral/unknown state rather than a fake reading

cdp-smoke (typr-e2e) reports 25/25 against the freshly built exe
